profile.reading: TierPoint provides colocation, cloud, and managed IT services from a portfolio the company and its majority owner describe as roughly 40 data centers across about 18 to 20 U.S. markets. This session traced and dated the companys ownership structure, previously recorded without a clear citation chain: institutional investor Argo Infrastructure Partners began investing in TierPoint in 2020, added a further 500 million dollars in 2022, and took a majority stake by 2024. Per Argos own December 9, 2025 press release, Argo then acquired the equity interests of most of TierPoints remaining minority shareholders, consolidating its control and bringing total capital formation under Argos ownership to 3 billion dollars since 2020. Separately, per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Apollo Global Management announced in January 2025 that it would acquire Argo Infrastructure Partners itself, adding about 6 billion dollars in assets to Apollos infrastructure platform, with closing expected in the second quarter of 2025, meaning Argos majority stake in TierPoint now sits within Apollos broader infrastructure platform. This specific row, recorded simply as TierPoint in Saint Louis, MO, could not be confidently matched to a specific building this session. The operators own Missouri data centers page, fetched fresh this session, lists three distinct Saint Louis area facilities: Millpark, at 2315 Millpark Drive, Suite 104, Maryland Heights, MO 63043, roughly 12 miles west of downtown, Olive, at 1111 Olive Street, St. Louis, MO 63101, downtown, and Locust, at 2300 Locust Street, St. Louis, MO 63103, also downtown. This rows own coordinates place it within the downtown core, which reasonably rules out the Maryland Heights Millpark building, but do not reliably distinguish between the closely spaced downtown Olive and Locust buildings without a precise geocoding tool, which was not available this session. A Baxtel listing uses the URL slug cosentry-st-louis-olive for the Olive building, suggesting it carries the older, Cosentry heritage lineage, while Data Center Dynamics and local St. Louis Post-Dispatch coverage describe Locust as a newer, separately announced office to data center conversion project valued up to 150 million dollars. Given genuine ambiguity between two plausible, similarly downtown buildings, no specific address is asserted for this row. A future researcher with access to precise parcel level geocoding could likely resolve which of the Olive or Locust buildings this specific row represents.
